title: How a lecture PDF becomes stored MCQs (5-stage pipeline)
purpose: Show every step that runs when a user uploads a lecture PDF: which scripts execute, what data flows between them, where each piece lands in the database, and what happens when something fails. The teacher should be able to point at any arrow and ask 'what is being passed here?' and find the answer.
audience: non-engineer teammates and the grading teacher

groups.label: Stage 3 — find the learning objectives (Claude call #1)
Stage 4 — generate MCQs per slide batch (Claude call #2, runs in batches of 10)
Orchestrator (lecture_ingest.py) — the conductor that runs all 5 stages

nodes.label: Lecture PDF
nodes.description: Uploaded by the user from the My Classes page

nodes.label: pdf_to_md_v3.extract_with_tables
nodes.description: Converts the PDF into Markdown and inserts a '--- PAGE N ---' marker between every slide so the next stage knows where each slide ends

nodes.label: page_splitter.split_lecture_md
nodes.description: Splits the Markdown on the PAGE markers; returns one record per slide ({page_number, raw_md})

nodes.label: page_splitter.batch_slides (size=10)
nodes.description: Groups slides into batches of 10 (D-4.3) so each MCQ call stays manageable

nodes.label: Factsheet subset (7 keys, D-1.2)
nodes.description: Built by _build_factsheet_subset — only 7 keys from the cleaned factsheet are passed to Claude (saves ~40% input tokens)

nodes.label: lo_extractor.extract_los
nodes.description: One Claude call per lecture. Asks Claude to list the lecture's learning objectives, the page range each one covers, and which pages should be ignored (title slides, dividers, etc.)

nodes.label: mcq_generator.generate_mcqs
nodes.description: One Claude call per batch of slides (≤10). Returns 1–3 MCQs per kept slide; multi-correct allowed (D-2.5); empty array means 'this slide isn't quiz-worthy' (D-4.8)

nodes.label: _validate_mcq
nodes.description: Defensive schema check — every MCQ must have 4 options, 4 rationales, and at least one valid correct index

nodes.label: queries_lectures.insert_lecture
nodes.description: Inserts the lectures row up front with status='pending'

nodes.label: queries_pages.insert_slide_page
nodes.description: One row per slide. status='kept' (with LO bound), 'ignored' (skipped page), or 'pending' (no LO covers this page — D-1.5 defensive)

nodes.label: queries_pages.set_slide_page_status
nodes.description: Re-flags slides after the MCQ stage: 'ignored' if Claude returned empty mcqs (D-4.8); 'pending' if the whole batch failed twice

nodes.label: queries_questions.insert_question
nodes.description: One row per validated MCQ. Computes difficulty_word_count now; the other 6 difficulty features stay NULL until Phase 4

nodes.label: queries_lectures.set_lecture_status
nodes.description: Final flip: 'ready' if every batch succeeded, 'pending' if any batch failed twice

nodes.label: lecture_ingest.ingest_lecture
nodes.description: Public entry point. Wires the 5 stages together and applies all the failure policies (D-4.4 retry, D-4.5 partial-success, D-4.7 LO failure halts MCQs, D-4.8 empty mcqs → ignored)

nodes.label: _call_with_retry (D-4.4)
nodes.description: Every Claude call goes through here: 2 attempts, no backoff, no third try

edges.description: The LO call sees the WHOLE lecture in one go — not the per-slide chunks
2-attempt retry. If both fail, lecture stays 'pending' and MCQs are skipped entirely (D-4.7)
One Claude call per batch — sequentially, not in parallel
MCQs are only generated for slides whose page is in an LO range and not in ignored_pages
2-attempt retry per batch. If a batch fails both attempts, those slides flip to 'pending' but the next batch still runs (D-4.5 partial success)
Every slide is persisted, with status set from the LO response
Only validated MCQs get inserted; invalid ones are logged and skipped

verification: All 5 D-4.2 stages appear as groups (extract → split → understand → generate → persist)
Both Claude calls (lo_extractor, mcq_generator) are shown as kind=claude_call
The retry helper is shown as connecting to BOTH Claude calls
The 4 failure-policy decisions are documented in node descriptions: D-4.4 (retry), D-4.5 (partial success), D-4.7 (LO failure halts MCQs), D-4.8 (empty mcqs → ignored)
The factsheet subset (7 keys, D-1.2) is shown as an input to the LO call
Every queries_* function the orchestrator calls is shown as a db_write node
No labeled connectors — relationship meaning lives in sticky notes / node descriptions
